docs.title: Signalith documentation
docs.text: Open-source SIEM · Apache 2.0

docs.title: Signalith documentation
docs.text:
Signalith collects logs from Windows, Linux, network devices and OpenTelemetry, stores them in OpenSearch, and adds the security layer on top: a pipe-based query language, scheduled detections with a triage queue, Sigma rule import, risk-based alerting, threat intel, dashboards and investigation cases. It is one Go program with the web UI built in, running as a Windows service, a systemd unit or a container.

Get started See the roadmap GitHub

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• Getting started

    Run it with Docker in two commands, or install it on Linux or Windows next to OpenSearch.

    Install and first steps

  • Data intake

    Fluent Bit agents for Windows and Linux, syslog and CEF from network devices, and OpenTelemetry logs over OTLP.

    Agents and syslog

  • Search

    A query language that reads like SPL, plain-English questions that become queries, and a visual builder.

    Query language

  • Detect and triage

    Scheduled detections mapped to MITRE ATT&CK, Sigma import, a findings queue, risk scores and threat intel matching.

    Detections

  • Dashboards

    The security posture dashboard and dashboards of your own, kept as YAML files you can review in Git.

    Dashboards

  • Try it with sample data

    A week of made-up activity for a fictional company, with attacks hidden in it. One click loads it, one click removes it.

    Sample data

  • Administration

    Settings, users and roles, Active Directory sign-in, several servers sharing one OpenSearch, and data retention.

    Server settings

  • Security

    HTTPS by default, encrypted secrets, a secured OpenSearch, and a built-in check of how your server is set up.

    Security checks

  • Roadmap

    What is done, what is being built now, and what comes after.

    Roadmap

docs.title: How it fits together
docs.text:
Fluent Bit agents ──HTTPS──▶ signalith (Go) ──REST──▶ OpenSearch
 (Windows, Linux)            ingest, parse,          events by data model and day
syslog devices ─UDP/TCP/TLS▶ query compiler,
OTLP collectors ──HTTPS────▶ web UI and API ◀── analyst browser

Signalith is a personal open-source project by Samuel Sanchez Jr., licensed under Apache 2.0. Questions, bug reports and ideas are welcome on GitHub; see Contributing to help out, and the security policy to report a weakness privately.

docs.title: Agent tokens
docs.text:
Agents (Fluent Bit, the OpenTelemetry Collector and osquery) prove who they are with an agent token, sent as Authorization: Bearer <token>. Each agent, or each group of agents that do the same job, gets its own token. You can see which token every event came with, and you can revoke one group without touching the others.

Tokens are listed on the Add data page, under Agent tokens. Admins can create, rename and revoke them there or with signalith tokens. Analysts can list their names through the API; nobody can see a token again after it is created.

docs.title: How tokens work
docs.text:
• Shape. A token is sgl_ followed by 52 lowercase letters and digits (a to z, 2 to 7), 56 characters in all, for example sgl_7f2kq…. The 52 characters hold 32 random bytes. The sgl_ prefix lets secret scanners (GitHub secret scanning, gitleaks, trufflehog and the like) find a token that leaked into a file or a chat. The pattern to give them is:
\bsgl_[a-z2-7]{52}\b
  • Shown once. Signalith shows a new token only when it creates it. It keeps the SHA-256 hash of the token, a 12-character ID (the start of that hash) and the last 4 characters (shown as sgl_…x7q2, so you can match a configuration file to a row). A plain SHA-256 is enough here: a token holds 256 random bits, so nobody can work it out from its hash. Lost a token? Create a new one and revoke the old one.
  • Shared by every server. Tokens are kept in OpenSearch, in the <prefix>_runtime index (signalith_runtime by default) that the servers of one Signalith share, so a token made on one server works on all of them. Only hashes are stored there.
  • Revocation takes seconds. Each server keeps the list in memory and checks OpenSearch every 2 seconds for a change. A revoked token is refused at once on the server where you revoked it, and within a few seconds on the others. No restart is needed.
  • When OpenSearch is down. Servers keep using the list they already have. Nothing can be revoked or created until OpenSearch is back, and no events can be stored either, so the list being a little old changes nothing. A server that starts while OpenSearch is down can't read the list yet: agents with an sgl_ token are asked to try again later (503, Retry-After: 30). Fluent Bit and the Collector keep their events and send them again. Agents with a shared token are asked the same, since you may have chosen Stop accepting on it: a token you turned away is never let back in.
  • Shared token IDs. A shared token (see below) is often one a person typed, so its ID is not made from a plain hash of it, which anyone who can search events could use to test guesses. It is an HMAC-SHA256 of the token under a random key kept in the <prefix>_runtime index, made the first time a server with a shared token reads the tokens.
  • Not a password. An agent token can't be used to sign in to the web UI or the API, and a user's password or session can't be used to send events.

docs.title: Create a token
docs.text:
On the Add data page (the usual way). Pick the source (Linux, Windows, OpenTelemetry or osquery) and type a name under Token for these agents, such as Linux web servers. The name is recorded on every event those agents send. The setup shows where the token goes. When you choose Copy or Download for the configuration, or copy a command that holds the token, Signalith creates the token, puts it in the configuration and the steps, and shows Created token "Linux web servers". Copy or download the configuration before you leave the page: the token is not shown again. Copying again reuses the same token; changing the name or the source makes a new one on the next copy.

Already have a token for these agents? Choose Use a token I already have and paste it.

Without a configuration. Under Agent tokens, choose New token, type a name and choose Create token. Copy the token from the next screen into the agent's configuration. When you choose Done, it is gone from the page.

From the command line: sudo signalith tokens create "Linux web servers" (see Commands).

Names are 1 to 64 letters, digits, spaces or . _ - ( ) / : # @, and no two active tokens can have the same name (capitals don't count). There can be up to 1,000 active tokens.

docs.title: Revoke a token
docs.text:
On Add data, under Agent tokens, open the token's ⋯ menu and choose Revoke, or run sudo signalith tokens revoke <id or name>.

  • Agents that send with it are refused within a few seconds on every server, with 401 and this agent token was revoked; give the agent a new configuration from the Add data page. The Health page names them.
  • osquery hosts enrolled with it are removed (see osquery hosts).
  • Events already stored stay, and keep the token's name.
  • It can't be undone. To bring those agents back, give them a new configuration from Add data.

Revoked tokens stay in the list under Show revoked, so old events still explain themselves. Rename in the same menu changes the name on new events only; events already stored keep the old name.

docs.title: What each event records
docs.text:
Signalith adds four fields to every event agents send:

Field Holds signalith_intake How it came in: agent (Fluent Bit, POST /api/ingest), otlp (OpenTelemetry), osquery or syslog signalith_token The token's name when the event arrived, such as Linux web servers (never the token itself). A shared token shows as Shared token 3f9c0a signalith_token_id The token's 12-character ID, which stays the same when the token is renamed signalith_sender The address that sent it, without the port. Behind a trusted proxy, the real client's address

Syslog has no token, so syslog events record only signalith_intake and signalith_sender.

For example, to see which agents sent with a token in the last day:

signalith_token="Linux web servers" | stats count by signalith_sender, host

Names a sender can't set. These fields are Signalith's own. Whatever a sender puts in an event, Signalith drops (and counts in dropped_fields, with a warning in the server log). The event itself is kept:

  • @timestamp, datamodel, device_time and dropped_fields;
  • signalith, and every name that starts with signalith_ or signalith.;
  • any name whose part before the first . is one of those, such as datamodel.x.

Capitals don't count (Signalith_Sample is dropped too). This covers OpenTelemetry attributes named signalith.* and signalith_sample, which marks sample data.

docs.title: Replace a shared token
docs.text:
Before per-agent tokens, every agent used the same token, from ingest.tokens in signalith.yaml or from SIGNALITH_INGEST_TOKEN or SIGNALITH_INGEST_TOKEN_FILE. The Docker quick start makes one too (ingest-token, made by its setup step). These shared tokens still work, so nothing breaks when you update. They are shown under Agent tokens as Shared tokens, with a warning: a copy taken from any one agent works for all of them, and you can't turn one agent away without turning all of them away. The Security page flags them too.

To replace a shared token:

  1. Open Add data and, for each group of agents, copy or download a new configuration. Each group gets its own token. Put the configuration on the agents and restart them.
  2. Under Agent tokens, watch the shared token's Last used. It covers every server. Once it is older than the last agent you updated, nothing uses it any more.

  3. Choose Stop accepting on the shared token. Every server refuses it within a few seconds, with no restart. Fluent Bit and the Collector drop the batches refused this way, so update the agents first. Changed your mind? Accept again undoes it. That's all. A token that is no longer accepted can't be used, and the Security page counts it as retired. It stays listed as No longer accepted.

  4. Docker quick start: stop here. Leave docker-compose.yml as it is, so git pull keeps updating it cleanly. On a new install no agent has the shared token, so you can choose Stop accepting on it straight away.

  5. signalith.yaml (optional): to tidy up, delete its line under ingest.tokens, then restart Signalith.
  6. Environment (optional): remove SIGNALITH_INGEST_TOKEN (or _FILE) from the service's environment and restart it.

Once servers that share one OpenSearch share their settings (see Settings), every server accepts the shared tokens of every server, and Add data names the server whose signalith.yaml or environment brought each one. Removing a token from a file or the environment then no longer stops it being accepted: Stop accepting on Add data is the only way to retire it, and every server follows it within seconds.

The example token change-this-ingest-token from older Docker quick starts is handled on its own; see The Docker quick start's old example token.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Run these on a Signalith server, as the user that can read signalith.yaml (usually with sudo). They use the OpenSearch in the configuration, so they work from any server of a cluster. Add -c <file> for another configuration file. In Docker, run them in the container: docker compose -f deploy/docker/docker-compose.yml exec signalith signalith tokens list.

signalith tokens list                      # active tokens and shared tokens; -all adds revoked ones, -json for scripts
signalith tokens create "Linux web servers"            # prints the token once, on its own line
signalith tokens create -purpose windows "Domain controllers"
signalith tokens rename 3f9c0a1b2c4d "Web servers (Leeds)"
signalith tokens revoke 3f9c0a1b2c4d       # or the exact name; asks first, -yes skips the question
signalith tokens legacy refuse a1b2c3d4e5f6   # stop accepting a shared token
signalith tokens legacy accept a1b2c3d4e5f6   # accept it again

create prints only the token on standard output, so TOKEN=$(signalith tokens create "Build agents") works; what it did goes to standard error. Changes made here are logged as audit lines (audit=true, by=cli:<your user>), as the same changes on the page are.

signalith secrets set ingest.tokens still adds a shared token, for setups that need one fixed token in the configuration. New agents should get their own token instead.

docs.title: API
docs.text:
Route Role Does GET /api/agent-tokens Analyst Lists tokens and shared tokens: name, status, created, last used, events in the last hour. Never a token POST /api/agent-tokens Admin {"name": "Linux servers", "purpose": "linux"} creates a token. purpose is linux, windows, otel, osquery or empty. The 201 answer is the only one that holds the token, in secret PATCH /api/agent-tokens/{id} Admin {"name": "New name"} renames it POST /api/agent-tokens/{id}/revoke Admin Revokes it; answers hosts_removed, the osquery hosts removed with it POST /api/agent-tokens/legacy/{id}/refuse Admin Stops accepting a shared token POST /api/agent-tokens/legacy/{id}/accept Admin Accepts it again

Errors carry error (a sentence), code and, for the name, field: "name": name_invalid, name_taken, purpose_invalid, not_found, revoked, too_many, rate_limited (more than 10 tokens a minute; wait for Retry-After), store_unavailable (OpenSearch can't be reached) and tokens_loading. Create, rename, revoke, stop accepting and accept again are written to the audit log, never with the token.

docs.title: osquery hosts
docs.text:
Hosts running osquery (see endpoints.md) enroll with an agent token as their enroll secret, and each host remembers which token it enrolled with. The setup script Add data makes for osquery holds a token of its own, named osquery hosts unless you choose another name.

  • Revoking that token, or choosing Stop accepting on a shared token, removes every host enrolled with it, on every server. Their next request is refused, and they must enroll again with an active token. The revoke answer and the message after it say how many hosts were removed.
  • A host enrolled with a shared token that was later deleted from signalith.yaml or the environment is refused too, since the token it enrolled with no longer exists.
  • Events from osquery record the token and the host's address as above, with signalith_intake=osquery.

docs.title: AI tools (MCP)
docs.text:
signalith mcp is a read-only Model Context Protocol server. It lets AI tools such as Claude Desktop, Claude Code, VS Code or Cursor look things up in Signalith while you chat: run searches, and read findings, cases, detections, assets and risk.

It cannot change anything. It has no tool that writes, it sends only reads to Signalith's API, and it signs in as a Signalith user, so that user's role decides what it can see.

docs.title: What the AI tool can do
docs.text:
Tool What it does whoami Shows the Signalith user and role the tools read as query_help Explains the query language and lists the data models and their fields check_query Checks a query without running it search Runs a search (50 rows by default, 500 at most) list_findings, get_finding, findings_summary The findings queue, one finding in full, and counts by status and severity list_cases, get_case Investigation cases list_detections, get_detection Detections, filtered by text, severity, ATT&CK technique or whether they are on list_assets, lookup_entity The asset and identity lists, and the context of one host or user risk_objects, risk_object The riskiest users and systems, and the risk events of one intel_lookup Whether a value is a known threat intel indicator

Every tool needs only the Viewer role. Long values and long lists are cut short so that one large event does not fill the model's context.

docs.title: 1. Make a user for the AI tool
docs.text:
Give the AI tool its own Signalith user, so you can see what it does in the audit log and turn it off on its own.

  1. In Signalith, open Settings > Users and click Add user.
  2. Name it, for example ai-assistant, and give it the Viewer role.
  3. If the user must choose a new password at their next sign-in (a temporary password), sign in to Signalith once as that user in a private browser window and choose its password. The MCP server cannot sign in until the temporary password is replaced.

A directory (Active Directory or LDAP) account works too. See users.md.

docs.title: 2. Get the signalith program
docs.text:
The MCP server runs on the computer where the AI tool runs, not on the Signalith server.

  • Windows: download signalith-windows-amd64.exe from the latest release, for example to C:\Tools\signalith.exe.
  • Linux: download signalith-linux-amd64, save it as /usr/local/bin/signalith and run chmod +x /usr/local/bin/signalith.
  • Docker: see Running it with Docker.

On a computer with Signalith installed from a package, the signalith program is already there.

docs.title: 3. Trust Signalith's certificate
docs.text:
The MCP server checks Signalith's HTTPS certificate. If you already trust Signalith's certificate authority in your browser on this computer (see Trust the certificate), there is nothing to do on Windows.

Otherwise, download the CA from the link on Signalith's sign-in page (signalith-ca.crt) and point the MCP server at it with SIGNALITH_CA_FILE, as in the examples below.

docs.title: 4. Check the settings
docs.text:
In PowerShell:

$env:SIGNALITH_URL = "https://siem.example.com:8080"
$env:SIGNALITH_USER = "ai-assistant"
$env:SIGNALITH_PASSWORD = "the password"
C:\Tools\signalith.exe mcp -check

On Linux:

SIGNALITH_URL=https://siem.example.com:8080 SIGNALITH_USER=ai-assistant \
SIGNALITH_PASSWORD='the password' signalith mcp -check

It prints the user and role it signed in as, or says what is wrong.

docs.title: 5. Add it to your AI tool
Claude Desktop
docs.text:
Open Settings > Developer > Edit Config in Claude Desktop. That opens claude_desktop_config.json (on Windows, %APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json). Add Signalith under mcpServers:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "signalith": {
      "command": "C:\\Tools\\signalith.exe",
      "args": ["mcp"],
      "env": {
        "SIGNALITH_URL": "https://siem.example.com:8080",
        "SIGNALITH_USER": "ai-assistant",
        "SIGNALITH_PASSWORD": "the password"
      }
    }
  }
}

Add "SIGNALITH_CA_FILE": "C:\\Users\\you\\Downloads\\signalith-ca.crt" to env if you needed it in step 3. Quit and restart Claude Desktop. Signalith's tools then show under the tools button in the chat box. Try asking "Which users had the most failed logins in Signalith in the last day?"

docs.title: Claude Code
docs.text:
claude mcp add signalith \
  --env SIGNALITH_URL=https://siem.example.com:8080 \
  --env SIGNALITH_USER=ai-assistant \
  --env SIGNALITH_PASSWORD='the password' \
  -- signalith mcp

docs.title: Other AI tools
docs.text: Any tool that runs local (stdio) MCP servers works: give it the command signalith with the argument mcp, and the settings below as environment variables.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Each setting can be a flag or an environment variable.

Flag Environment variable Meaning -url SIGNALITH_URL Signalith's web address, such as https://siem.example.com:8080. Plain http:// is refused except to localhost, since it would send the password unencrypted -user SIGNALITH_USER The Signalith user to read as SIGNALITH_PASSWORD That user's password -password-file SIGNALITH_PASSWORD_FILE A file holding the password, instead of SIGNALITH_PASSWORD -ca SIGNALITH_CA_FILE A PEM file of a certificate authority to trust, besides the system's -check Check the settings, print the user and exit

The password is not taken as a flag, so it does not show in process lists.

docs.title: Running it with Docker
docs.text:
The Signalith image runs the MCP server too. In the AI tool's config, use docker as the command:

"signalith": {
  "command": "docker",
  "args": ["run", "-i", "--rm",
           "-e", "SIGNALITH_URL", "-e", "SIGNALITH_USER", "-e", "SIGNALITH_PASSWORD",
           "ghcr.io/jrsamsanchez/signalith:main", "mcp"],
  "env": {
    "SIGNALITH_URL": "https://siem.example.com:8080",
    "SIGNALITH_USER": "ai-assistant",
    "SIGNALITH_PASSWORD": "the password"
  }
}

To trust Signalith's CA, mount it and name it: "-v", "C:\\Users\\you\\Downloads\\signalith-ca.crt:/ca.crt:ro", "-e", "SIGNALITH_CA_FILE=/ca.crt". A Signalith server on the same computer is https://host.docker.internal:8080 from inside the container.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Read only. The MCP server sends only GET requests, plus searches and query checks, to Signalith. It refuses to send anything else, whatever the user's role allows.
  • The user's role applies. Signalith checks every request against the user's role, as for a person. A Viewer account is enough for every tool.
  • What the model sees goes to its provider. Search results, findings and cases the model reads are sent to whoever runs the model, like anything else in the chat. Unlike Investigate with AI, nothing is masked first. Use a model you are allowed to send this data to, or one you run yourself.
  • Event data is untrusted. Logs can hold text an attacker wrote, such as a user name or a command line made to look like instructions. The server tells the model never to follow instructions in data, and because every tool only reads, such text cannot make the tools change anything. Still check what the model tells you against Signalith itself before you act on it.
  • The password is in the AI tool's config file. Keep that file private. To cut the AI tool off, disable its user on Settings > Users.
  • Audit. Requests show in Signalith's log under the AI tool's user, with the user agent signalith-mcp/<version>.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Message What to do Signalith did not accept the username and password Check SIGNALITH_USER and SIGNALITH_PASSWORD. Too many wrong passwords lock the account for a while; see users.md This Signalith user must choose a new password first Sign in to Signalith once as this user in a browser and choose a password (step 1) certificate signed by unknown authority Trust Signalith's CA, or set SIGNALITH_CA_FILE (step 3) could not reach Signalith Check the address and port, and that this computer can reach the server (try the address in a browser) This needs the Analyst role Not expected for these tools; check that the server runs the same Signalith version

Claude Desktop keeps each MCP server's messages in its logs: on Windows in %APPDATA%\Claude\logs\mcp-server-signalith.log.

docs.title: Antivirus logs
docs.text:
Signalith collects what your antivirus finds and does: malware it found and whether it removed it, protection rules that blocked something, and the health of the antivirus itself (turned off, exclusions added, definitions out of date). Every antivirus event goes into the Malware data model (datamodel=Malware, kept in the <index_prefix>-malware-YYYY.MM.DD indices and listed as Malware on the Data retention page). The built-in Malware dashboard shows it at a glance, and eight built-in detections raise findings for malware that was not removed, outbreaks across several hosts, ransomware, and antivirus being turned off or given exclusions.

Three ways in:

Product How it gets here Set up Microsoft Defender Antivirus The Windows agent, with no extra setup Microsoft Defender ClamAV The Linux agent ClamAV Symantec, Trend Micro, Sophos, Trellix (McAfee) ePO, ESET, CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, Kaspersky, Bitdefender and any product that sends CEF or LEEF Syslog from the product's management console Antivirus consoles

The steps for each, with this server's address and ports filled in, are on Add data › Antivirus in the web UI.

docs.title: Microsoft Defender
docs.text:
The Windows agent reads the Microsoft-Windows-Windows Defender/Operational event log next to the Security log, so every host with the agent sends its Defender events. Hosts without Defender (for example Server Core with the feature removed) are skipped quietly: the agent still starts and still sends the Security log.

Event IDs What it means type action 1006, 1116 Malware or unwanted software found threat detected 1015 Suspicious behaviour found threat detected (category behavior) 1007, 1117 Defender acted on it threat what it did: quarantined, deleted, cleaned, blocked or allowed 1008, 1118, 1119 Defender tried to act on it and failed threat failed (reason says why) 1009 A file was restored from quarantine threat restored 1121, 1122 An attack surface reduction rule blocked or audited something rule blocked, audited 1123, 1124, 1127, 1128 Controlled folder access blocked or audited a change rule blocked, audited 1125, 1126 Network protection blocked or audited a web address rule audited, blocked 2000, 2002 Definitions or engine updated health updated 2001, 2003, 2004, 2006 Definitions, engine or platform update failed health update_failed 3002, 5008 Real-time protection or the engine failed health engine_failed 5000, 5009, 5011 Protection turned on health enabled 5001, 5010, 5012 Protection turned off health disabled 5004 A real-time protection setting changed health modified 5007 A setting changed: an exclusion added or removed, protection turned off by a setting, or anything else health exclusion_added, exclusion_removed, disabled or modified 5013 Tamper protection blocked a change health tamper_blocked 1150, 1151 Defender's regular health report; 1151 with definitions 7 or more days old health status, or outdated

Other Defender event IDs are kept in the Other data model, searchable with sourcetype="WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Windows Defender/Operational".

docs.title: Updating an agent installed before antivirus support
docs.text:
Fluent Bit does not fetch its configuration, so an agent set up before this version keeps sending the Security log only. On Add data › Windows, download the configuration again, copy it over C:\Program Files\fluent-bit\conf\fluent-bit.conf, then in PowerShell as administrator run:

Restart-Service fluent-bit

docs.title: ClamAV
docs.text:
The Linux agent reads ClamAV's own log files, /var/log/clamav/*.log (clamav.log from the scanner daemon, freshclam.log from the updater and clamonacc.log from on-access scanning). It sends:

  • FOUND lines: malware found, with the file and, when ClamAV gives them, its MD5 and size;
  • moved to, Removed. and Can't move/Can't remove lines: what happened to the file. By default clamd, clamonacc and clamdscan only report what they find, so a FOUND line with none of these after it means the file is still on the host, and raises the high malware-left-clamav finding. To have ClamAV move what it finds, run clamdscan with --move=/var/lib/clamav/quarantine, or set OnAccessPrevention yes for on-access scanning;
  • freshclam updates and update errors, and ClamAV's warning that its definitions are more than 7 days old.

Its routine SelfCheck lines are dropped at the agent.

Red Hat, Rocky, AlmaLinux and Fedora run ClamAV with logging to the system journal instead of /var/log/clamav. On Add data › Linux, choose Read from: systemd journal; the agent then also reads the journal entries of clamd, clamonacc and freshclam.

Only clamd, clamonacc and freshclam write logs. A plain clamscan run prints to the terminal and writes no log, so scan with clamdscan (which asks clamd) to have results reach Signalith.

docs.title: Updating an agent installed before antivirus support
docs.text:
On Add data › Linux, download the configuration again, then put it in place and restart the agent:

sudo install -m 600 -o root -g root fluent-bit.conf /etc/fluent-bit/fluent-bit.conf && sudo systemctl restart fluent-bit

docs.title: Antivirus consoles over syslog
docs.text:
Most endpoint protection products send events from their management console rather than from each computer. Point the console at Signalith's syslog receiver (see Syslog for turning it on). Add data › Antivirus has the steps for each product with your address and port filled in; consoles send over TCP when it is on, otherwise UDP.

Product Format Where to turn it on Symantec Endpoint Protection Symantec's own (SymantecServer) Endpoint Protection Manager: Admin › Servers › Local Site › Configure External Logging; tick Risk on the Log Filter tab Trend Micro Apex One CEF Apex Central: Administration › Settings › Syslog Settings; log format CEF, log type Detections Trend Micro Deep Security CEF Deep Security Manager: a syslog configuration in CEF format, used for the policy's anti-malware events Sophos Central CEF Sophos's SIEM script (Sophos-Central-SIEM-Integration), run every 5 minutes on a Linux server Trellix (McAfee) ePO Trellix's own (XML) ePO: Menu › Configuration › Registered Servers › New Server › Syslog Server. Needs syslog over TLS ESET PROTECT LEEF More › Settings › Advanced Settings › Syslog server, then Export logs to Syslog in LEEF with Detections ticked CrowdStrike Falcon CEF The Falcon SIEM Connector on a Linux server, with output_format = cef SentinelOne CEF Settings › Integrations › Syslog, then tick Syslog for the threat notifications Kaspersky Security Center CEF Administration Server properties › SIEM (ArcSight, CEF format), then Export to SIEM system using Syslog on the threat events of the policy Bitdefender GravityZone CEF Bitdefender's Event Push connector, with syslog output in CEF Anything else CEF or LEEF The product's syslog or SIEM export

Trellix ePO only sends over TLS. Set syslog.tls (for example 0.0.0.0:6514) on the Settings page, register Signalith in ePO by a name or address its certificate covers, and click Test Connection. See docs/https.md for the certificate.

For any other product, Signalith files an event under Malware when the event names the threat (a custom string labelled Threat Name, Virus Name, Malware Name, Detection Name or Risk Name, for example cs1Label=Threat Name cs1=Trojan.Agent), or when its category says virus or malware and it names a file. A threat name of None, N/A, - or unknown doesn't count. Web proxies, firewalls and mail gateways (such as Zscaler, which sends threatname=None with every web request) stay where they are, and so do web requests from products that don't call themselves antivirus. Everything else stays searchable in Network_Traffic or Other, with sourcetype=cef or sourcetype=leef.

For console events, dest is the computer the event is about (from the event's destination or computer name), not the console that sent it.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
Every Malware event has type and action, and a signature: the threat name for threats (Unknown threat when the product gave none), the rule name for rules, and a plain event name such as Antivirus exclusion added for health events. The common fields _time, host, sourcetype, vendor_product, signature_id (the Defender event ID, or the product's event ID) and _raw are there too.

type Meaning action values threat Malware or unwanted software was found detected, blocked, quarantined, deleted, cleaned, allowed, failed, restored rule A protection rule acted (attack surface reduction, controlled folder access, network protection) blocked, audited health The antivirus itself changed or has a problem disabled, enabled, exclusion_added, exclusion_removed, modified, update_failed, updated, outdated, engine_failed, tamper_blocked, status

Malware not removed means action IN (allowed, failed, restored): the antivirus left the file alone, failed to clean it, or someone restored it from quarantine. The detections, the dashboard and the Ask box all use this set.

Field Description Example type Kind of event: threat (malware found), rule (a protection rule acted) or health (the antivirus itself changed or has a problem) threat action What happened, such as quarantined, failed, disabled or exclusion_added quarantined vendor_action The action as the product wrote it Quarantine threat_id The product's ID for the threat 2147729891 category Kind of threat: virus, worm, trojan, ransomware, backdoor, spyware, adware, pua, exploit, hacktool, behavior, test or other trojan vendor_category The threat category as the product wrote it Tool severity How serious the product rates it: low, medium, high or critical high vendor_severity The severity as the product wrote it Severe dest Host the event is about ws-fin-07 dest_ip Address of that host, when the product sends one 192.0.2.27 user Account involved, such as the user who opened the file CORP\alice.nguyen src Address the threat came from, when the product says 203.0.113.45 src_host Host the threat came from, when the product says file-01 url Web address the threat came from or was blocked at file_name File name of the threat invoice.exe file_path Full path of the threat C:\Users\alice.nguyen\Downloads\invoice.exe file_hash File hash as the product sent it file_md5, file_sha1, file_sha256 The hash split by kind, lower case file_size File size in bytes 68 process Command line of the process involved process_name Executable file name of the process involved winword.exe process_path Executable path of the process involved process_id Process ID 4120 rule Protection rule that acted Office app started a child process rule_id ID of that rule (for attack surface reduction, its GUID) d4f940ab-401b-4efc-aadc-ad5f3c50688a setting Setting that changed, as the product wrote it exclusion What an added or removed exclusion lets through C:\ProgramData\SyncSvc exclusion_type Kind of exclusion: path, extension, process or ip path signature_version Version of the antivirus definitions 1.419.2361.0 engine_version Version of the scan engine 1.1.24090.11 product_version Version of the antivirus product 4.18.24090.11 signature_age_days Age of the definitions in days, when the product reports it 9 reason Error or reason text from the product The process cannot access the file detection_source Which scan or feature found it Real-Time Protection

The file_md5, file_sha1 and file_sha256 fields are checked against threat intel hashes by threatmatch and intel (see threat-intel.md).

docs.title: Searching
docs.text:
To find Search Malware the antivirus did not remove, by host datamodel=Malware type=threat action IN (allowed, failed, restored) \| stats count by dest, signature The same threat on several hosts datamodel=Malware type=threat category!=test \| stats dc(dest) as hosts, count by signature \| where hosts >= 2 \| sort -hosts Exclusions added, and what they let through datamodel=Malware type=health action=exclusion_added \| table _time, dest, user, exclusion_type, exclusion Hosts whose definitions are old or failing to update datamodel=Malware type=health action IN (outdated, update_failed) \| stats count by dest, vendor_product, signature \| sort -count Attack surface reduction blocks by rule datamodel=Malware type=rule action=blocked \| stats count, dc(dest) as hosts by rule \| sort -count Everything the antivirus said about one host datamodel=Malware dest=ws-fin-07 \| table _time, type, action, signature, file_path, user

The Ask box understands questions such as malware not removed in the last 7 days, hosts where antivirus was turned off and asr blocks by rule.

docs.title: Detections
docs.text:
All ten are on by default. Edit or turn them off on the Detections page.

ID Severity What it means What to do malware-not-removed high Antivirus found malware but did not remove it: the clean-up failed, someone allowed the file, or it was restored from quarantine. Open the host's events around this time to see whether the file ran. Run a full scan, remove the file by hand or reimage the host. If someone allowed the file on purpose, check that it really is safe. malware-left-clamav high ClamAV found malware but only reported it, so the file is still on the host. Search datamodel=Malware dest="<the host>" file_path="<the path>" for the threat's name. Remove or quarantine the file by hand, then find out how it got there. To have ClamAV move what it finds, see ClamAV. malware-detected low Antivirus found malware. Most products block, quarantine, delete or clean it straight away; when one did not, malware-not-removed or malware-left-clamav is raised as well. Ransomware has its own finding. Check where the file came from (file_path, url, user). Repeated finds on one host, or the same threat on other hosts, mean something keeps bringing it back. An EICAR detection (category test) is someone testing the antivirus; close it as benign. malware-outbreak high The same threat was found on three or more hosts within a day. Test files, adware and potentially unwanted apps are left out. Search datamodel=Malware signature="<the threat>" to list the hosts and file paths. A common path (a file share, a download folder) or a common sender shows where it spreads from. malware-ransomware critical Antivirus found ransomware. Even when it was removed, more may be running or waiting on the network. Isolate the host now. Check other hosts for the same threat and for shadow copy deletion, and check the file shares this user can write to. av-protection-disabled high Real-time protection, scanning or tamper protection was turned off. Ask who changed it. If another antivirus product was just installed, Defender turning itself off is expected; close this as benign. Otherwise turn protection back on and look at what ran on the host just before. av-tamper-blocked medium Tamper protection blocked an attempt to change the antivirus. The antivirus stayed on. Look at setting to see what was blocked. If it fires on many hosts after a Group Policy, Intune or SCCM change, the policy is fighting tamper protection; fix the policy and close these as benign. On a single host with no policy change, check what ran there just before. av-exclusion-added medium A folder, file type, process or address was excluded from antivirus scanning. Check the exclusion against your approved list. Exclusions for temporary, download or ProgramData folders, or for script hosts such as powershell.exe, are rarely legitimate. av-definitions-failing low Definitions failed to update at least twice in a day, or are a week or more old. Check that the host can reach its update source (proxy, firewall, disk space). Several hosts at once usually means the update server or mirror is down. av-rule-block medium A Windows protection rule (attack surface reduction or controlled folder access) blocked something that rarely happens in normal work, such as an Office document starting PowerShell. The block worked, but whatever tried it is still on the host. Look at process_name (what tried) and file_path (what it tried to start or change).

av-rule-block leaves out three attack surface reduction rules that also block routine software: Credential theft from LSASS, Rare or untrusted executable and Untrusted program from USB. They are still in the data (datamodel=Malware type=rule). The rules it covers map to these ATT&CK techniques:

Rule Technique Vulnerable signed driver T1068 Persistence through WMI event subscription T1546.003 Adobe Reader started a child process, Office app started a child process, Office app created executable content, Script launched downloaded executable content T1204.002 Executable content from email, Office communication app started a child process T1566.001 Obfuscated script T1027 Office app injected code into another process T1055 Process creation from PsExec or WMI T1047 Reboot into Safe Mode T1688 Copied or impersonated system tool T1036 Webshell creation on a server T1505.003 Office macro called Win32 APIs T1106 Ransomware protection, Controlled folder access T1486

Sigma rules with logsource: category: antivirus convert to datamodel=Malware searches (see detections.md).

docs.title: The Malware dashboard
docs.text:
Dashboards › Malware is built in and opens on the last 7 days:

Panel Shows Hosts with malware Hosts with any threat (EICAR tests left out), compared with the period before Hosts with malware not removed Hosts where a threat was allowed, failed to clean or was restored Hosts with protection off or tampered with Hosts where protection was turned off or tamper protection blocked a change Malware found over time, by what the antivirus did Threats per hour or day, one line per action Top threats The threats on the most hosts, and how often each was found Hosts with the most malware The hosts with the most threats Malware not removed Each threat not removed, with host, user and file Threats by category Trojan, ransomware, PUA and so on Events by product Which antivirus products are sending Protection rule blocks Attack surface reduction and controlled folder access blocks by rule Antivirus health problems Protection off, tampering, exclusions, failed updates, old definitions and engine failures, by host

Defender logs each threat twice, once when it finds it and once when it acts. The charts count only the second, so each threat counts once.

Until antivirus events arrive, the dashboard says so above its panels, with a button that opens Add data › Antivirus (for admins).

The dashboard can't be edited. To change it, choose Make a copy (analysts and admins, when custom dashboards are on): the copy, Malware (copy), is a custom dashboard you can edit, add panels to and delete. Download YAML saves its definition. See dashboards.md.

docs.title: Testing with the EICAR test file
docs.text:
The EICAR test file is a harmless file that every antivirus treats as malware, made for checking that detection works. Download it from eicar.org on a test host:

  • Microsoft Defender: download it in a browser. Defender removes it and the event shows in Search (datamodel=Malware) within a minute.
  • ClamAV: download it and scan it with clamdscan:
curl -fsSO https://secure.eicar.org/eicar.com.txt; clamdscan --fdpass eicar.com.txt; rm -f eicar.com.txt

The detection has category test, so it raises a low malware-detected finding (close it as benign) and does not count on the dashboard's malware panels. On ClamAV, clamdscan only reports the file unless you add --move or --remove, so the test also raises malware-left-clamav; the command above deletes the file afterwards, so close that one as benign too.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Nothing arrives. Search datamodel=Malware earliest=-1h. For agents, check the host on the Health page and that the agent runs (Get-Service fluent-bit or systemctl status fluent-bit). For consoles, open Add data › Syslog: the See it arrive box shows whether the console's address has sent anything, and anything turned away, such as a sender not in syslog.allow.

Defender events are missing but the Security log arrives. The agent still has its old configuration. Download it again and restart the agent (see Updating an agent). Search sourcetype="WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Windows Defender/Operational" to check.

ClamAV on Red Hat, Rocky, AlmaLinux or Fedora sends nothing. ClamAV logs to the journal there: choose Read from: systemd journal on Add data › Linux, download the configuration and restart the agent. Remember that clamscan writes no log; use clamdscan.

Console events land in Other or Network_Traffic instead of Malware. The event did not say it was about malware. Check the console sends its threat or detection events (not only audit or system events) in CEF or LEEF, and that each names the threat. Search sourcetype=cef or sourcetype=leef to see what arrived, and compare it with the format in Antivirus consoles.

Trellix ePO can't connect (Test Connection fails). ePO needs syslog over TLS: set syslog.tls on the Settings page and restart, allow that port (6514 by default) through the firewall, and register Signalith by a name or address Signalith's certificate covers (see docs/https.md).

docs.title: signalith cluster
docs.text:
The servers that share one OpenSearch keep the settings they share in it, in the <prefix>_config index, signed with the cluster key that each of them keeps in its state folder (see Shared settings and the cluster key). The server that runs the background jobs makes the cluster by itself, so most setups only ever need export-key and import-key, to give another server the key. The other commands are for when something went wrong.

Run the commands as the user Signalith runs as (on Linux packages, sudo -u signalith), on a server whose signalith.yaml names the OpenSearch the servers share. Every command takes -c <file> for another configuration file. Each change is written to the log as an audit record, with who ran it.

found and reset-key change the cluster without a running server's help; the others may run while Signalith runs on the same computer.

Command What it does status This server's place in the cluster, the servers with the key, and any problem export-key Writes the cluster key, encrypted with a passphrase, for another server import-key Gives this server the cluster key that export-key wrote export Prints the shared settings as YAML; with -settings, the settings of all servers as a file apply takes apply Changes the settings of all servers to those of a file (configuration as code) import -from-cache Writes this server's copy of the shared settings back to OpenSearch found Makes the cluster from this server's files reset-key Makes a new cluster key when every copy of it is lost accept-restore Accepts the shared settings after an OpenSearch snapshot was restored

signalith passwd, which is not a cluster command, changes the built-in admin's password for every server of a cluster that shares its users; see The built-in admin's password.

docs.title: status
docs.text:
signalith cluster status [-c file] [-json]

Shows this server's name and identity, its mode, the cluster's name, identity and level (3 once every server can read shared settings, 2 once every server can read shared users, 1 before), the cluster key it uses, the servers in the keyring and any problem, such as a shared setting that does not check out. -json prints the same as JSON, with the mode and the cluster under shared, and problems and warnings when there are any:

{
  "server": "siem-a",
  "node_id": "…",
  "shared": {"mode": "member", "cluster_id": "…", "cluster_name": "Signalith", "…": "…"},
  "keyring": {"…": {"name": "siem-a", "fingerprint": "…", "added_at": "…", "added_by": "…"}},
  "keys": ["…"]
}

The modes:

Mode Meaning member This server is a member of the cluster and reads the shared settings from OpenSearch importing It founded the cluster and is moving its files into OpenSearch legacy_b It is not part of the cluster yet, so it uses its own files and runs no background jobs: give it the cluster key legacy_c No cluster exists yet; it uses its own files until the server that runs the background jobs founds it legacy_a OpenSearch could not be reached and it has no copy of the shared settings, so it uses its own files degraded It cannot use the shared settings in OpenSearch now; it keeps the copy it has, and changes are paused key_missing The shared settings are signed with a cluster key this server does not have gone The shared settings in OpenSearch are gone: their index was deleted or replaced

docs.title: export-key and import-key
docs.text:
signalith cluster export-key [-c file] [-o file]
signalith cluster import-key [-c file] <file>

export-key asks for a passphrase of at least 12 characters and writes the cluster key, encrypted with it, to -o (readable by you only) or to the standard output. Copy the file to the other server and run import-key there with the same passphrase. The key is kept in that server's state folder, encrypted with its master key, and a running server joins the cluster within seconds. Delete the file afterwards.

When the standard input is not a terminal, both read the passphrase from its first line, so a script can pipe it in.

Instead of import-key, a key you chose before the cluster was made can be given in a file named in SIGNALITH_CLUSTER_KEY_FILE: 32 random bytes as one line of base64, such as openssl rand -base64 32 > cluster-key, readable by Signalith only. The server that makes the cluster uses that key, so only a cluster made with it can be joined this way; no command writes an existing cluster's key in plain form (see Shared settings and the cluster key).

docs.title: export
docs.text:
signalith cluster export [-c file] [-o file]

Prints every shared document as YAML: its kind, revision, who changed it last and its content. Stored passwords and API keys stay encrypted with the cluster key. Use it to look at the shared settings, or to keep a copy next to your backups. Documents in <prefix>_config that Signalith did not write are named in a comment and left out.

docs.title: export -settings
docs.text:
signalith cluster export -settings [-c file] [-o file] [-server name]

Once the servers share their settings (see Settings on several servers), writes the settings of all servers as one file in the shape of signalith.yaml, the file apply takes as it is, followed by each server's own settings as comments marked "this server only" (only one server's with -server, a name or node id). Passwords and keys are left out. It is the same file as Download settings as YAML on the Settings page.

docs.title: apply
docs.text:
signalith cluster apply [-c file] -f file [-yes]

Changes the settings every server shares to those of a file in the shape of signalith.yaml, such as one export -settings wrote and you then edited and keep in version control. It shows what changes, compared with the values in use, asks, and then writes them, as a change on the Settings page would: what applies at once does so on every server within a few seconds, and the Settings page lists what waits for a restart and restarts the servers one at a time. -yes skips the question, for scripts. Applying a file that changes nothing says so and writes nothing.

  • Only settings for all servers are taken. A file with a server's own settings, or its connection and folder settings, is refused with the list of them: change those on that server's Settings page. Settings not in the file are left as they are.
  • retention.*, intel.feeds and auth.ldap in the file change the shared retention policies, feeds and directory sign-in, as a change of them in a server's signalith.yaml would.
  • A changed auth.admin_user renames the built-in admin for every server: it signs in under the new name with the same password, and its sessions end. A user that already has the new name stops it. If the command is stopped part way, run it again to finish. This is the only way to rename it: a changed auth.admin_user in one server's signalith.yaml is only listed on the Servers page.
  • It refuses while the servers do not share their settings yet, or while this server cannot use the shared settings (it is not a member, or OpenSearch refuses writes).

Every change is audited with who ran the command.

docs.title: import -from-cache
docs.text:
signalith cluster import [-c file] -from-cache

Each server keeps its last copy of the shared settings in cluster/cache.enc in its state folder, encrypted with its master key. When the <prefix>_config index was deleted, every server says the shared settings are gone (and /readyz answers gone). Run this on the server whose copy is the newest: it writes the copy back, with the same cluster identity, and the other servers resume by themselves. Documents still in OpenSearch are left as they are. If OpenSearch holds another cluster by then, nothing is written.

A copy older than 30 days is not used.

docs.title: found
docs.text:
signalith cluster found [-c file] [-force] [-name name]

Makes the servers sharing this OpenSearch a cluster, from this server's files: its feeds and retention policies become the shared ones, and it makes the cluster key. The server that runs the background jobs does this by itself, so found refuses while a server that may run them is up (it watches the servers' heartbeats for 12 seconds to tell); -force founds anyway. -name names the cluster (Signalith by default).

If this server was a member of a cluster whose shared settings are gone, use import -from-cache instead, which keeps the cluster. When no server keeps a copy, found -force makes the cluster again from this server's files.

Give the other servers the new key afterwards (export-key, then import-key).

docs.title: reset-key
docs.text:
signalith cluster reset-key [-c file] [-yes]

When every copy of the cluster key is lost, nobody can check the shared settings any more. Stop every server first: reset-key refuses while one is up. It also refuses while this server still has a key the shared settings check out with (in its state folder or in SIGNALITH_CLUSTER_KEY_FILE): the key is not lost then, so give it to the other servers with export-key and import-key instead. It shows each shared document, with its revision, who changed it last, whether its signature checks out with a key this server has and how it compares to this server's copy, asks you to confirm (-yes skips the question), makes a new key and signs the documents with it. A document whose signature fails under a key this server has was changed outside Signalith: it is not signed again, so every server keeps ignoring it. Passwords and API keys stored with the old key cannot be read and are emptied; the command lists them, so you can enter them again on the Threat intel page. Then give the other servers the new key. Settings in a server's signalith.yaml that it already applied are not applied again because of the new key: each server records them afresh at its next start.

docs.title: accept-restore
docs.text:
signalith cluster accept-restore [-c file] [-yes]

Each server remembers how far the shared settings had got, and refuses older ones as changed outside Signalith. After you restore an OpenSearch snapshot on purpose, run this on a member of the cluster: every server accepts the shared settings now in OpenSearch within seconds.

docs.title: The built-in admin's password
docs.text:
signalith passwd [-c file] [-local]

On a server of a cluster whose servers share their users (see Users on several servers), signalith passwd asks for the new password twice and changes the built-in admin's password for every server of the cluster, in OpenSearch. It applies within a few seconds, with no restart, and is written to the log as an audit record. It needs the cluster key and OpenSearch, like the commands above. When OpenSearch cannot be reached, or the servers do not share their users yet, it changes the password in this server's files, as on a server that is not in a cluster, and says what that does: a password kept in admin-password-hash in the state folder is used only while this server keeps its users in its own files, and one written to signalith.yaml becomes the password of every server the next time this server starts with OpenSearch available. Run it again once OpenSearch answers to change the cluster's password at once.

-local keeps the new password on this server only, in admin-password-local in its state folder. On a server of a cluster that shares its users it works only while the shared settings cannot be used (OpenSearch down, or refusing writes because its disk is full), so an admin can always sign in to that server to fix it; it applies within a few seconds, with no restart. It is the only break-glass password: an admin-password-hash from an earlier signalith passwd is not one. Use it before you need it; it never changes the password of the other servers. On a server that was never in a cluster, -local writes admin-password-hash and needs a restart, as signalith passwd does there.

docs.title: When to use which
docs.text: What happened What to do A new server says it is not part of the cluster export-key on a member, import-key on it Someone deleted the <prefix>_config index import -from-cache on the server with the newest copy OpenSearch was restored from a snapshot accept-restore Every copy of the cluster key is lost Stop every server, reset-key, then export-key and import-key No server can run the background jobs, and you need the cluster now found The built-in admin's password is lost or must change on every server signalith passwd on any server You want a password for one server that works while OpenSearch is down signalith passwd -local on that server

docs.title: Code signing policy
docs.text:
Signalith's releases are signed so you can check that what you downloaded is exactly what the project built from its public source.

Download Signed with Windows installer (.msi) and signalith-windows-amd64.exe Authenticode, once Windows code signing is set up (below) Linux packages (.deb, .rpm) and the apt and dnf repositories The Signalith release GPG key, once it is set up Container images on GHCR Sigstore, with build provenance Every release file (through SHA256SUMS) Sigstore and GitHub build provenance (and GPG, once set up)

Check a download shows how to verify each one.

docs.title: Windows
docs.text:
Free code signing provided by SignPath.io, certificate by SignPath Foundation.

Until that is in place, the Windows files are not Authenticode-signed and Windows SmartScreen warns before running the installer; the checksums and their Sigstore signature still let you check them.

Only files built by the project's GitHub Actions Release workflow from a tagged commit in jrsamsanchez/Signalith are sent for signing, and a maintainer approves each signing request. Every signed file is named Signalith and carries the release's version.

docs.title: Team roles
docs.text:
• Committers and reviewers: the repository owner. Most code is written with Claude Code, an AI coding tool, through pull requests that must pass the project's tests before they are merged. Pull requests from other people are reviewed before they are merged.
  • Approvers: the repository owner approves each release and each signing request.

Everyone in these roles uses multi-factor authentication for GitHub and SignPath.

docs.title: Privacy
docs.text: Signalith does not send information to other networked systems unless you set it up to. It only connects to the systems you configure: your OpenSearch, the agents and devices that send it data, threat intel feeds you add, notification channels you add, an AI provider if you turn on the assistant (only the question is sent), directory servers for sign-in, and, if you choose Daily content updates (the default is Manual), the project's GitHub releases to check for newer detection rules. There is no telemetry.

docs.title: Reporting a problem
docs.text: To report a signed file that behaves maliciously, or any security problem, see the security policy.

docs.title: Dashboards
docs.text: The Dashboards tab has two built-in dashboards, Security posture and Malware, and any custom dashboards you build. Pick one from the list at the top left, choose a time range, and optionally turn on auto-refresh (every minute, 5 or 15 minutes; it pauses while the browser tab is hidden).

docs.title: Security posture
docs.text:
The built-in dashboard, like the Splunk ES Security Posture and executive summary dashboards. Every key number is compared with the previous period of the same length, so "Last 24 hours" compares today with the 24 hours before.

Panel What it shows Open findings Findings not yet resolved or closed, with a count per urgency New findings Findings raised in the period Findings closed Findings moved to resolved or closed in the period Mean time to triage From a finding being raised to its first status change or owner assignment, for findings triaged in the period Mean time to resolve From a finding being raised to it being resolved or closed, for findings closed in the period Events ingested Events stored in the period, all data models except Risk Findings over time by urgency New findings per hour (or per 15 minutes, 6 hours or day, depending on the range) Top detections firing Findings plus risk events per detection; click one to open it Top risk objects Users and systems with the most risk; click one to open it on the Risk page ATT&CK tactics seen Findings and risk events per ATT&CK tactic, in matrix order Detection health Enabled detections, detections whose last run failed, detections behind schedule, enabled detections with no findings and no risk events in 30 days, and data sources that stopped sending. When missed runs were skipped (older than detections.catch_up) in the period or the last day, a line says when, for example "Signalith was not running detections from 02:10 to 09:40; 90 runs of 'Brute force' were skipped". Every server shows the same health Events by data model, by source type Event volume over time

A data source is a host and source type pair. It counts as stopped when it sent events in the last 7 days but nothing for dashboards.stale_after (default 2h). Raise the setting for hosts that send in bursts:

dashboards:
  stale_after: 6h

Each section loads on its own: if one part fails (for example, OpenSearch rejects a query), that card shows the error and the rest of the dashboard still works. Cards with an Open in Search link show the exact query behind them.

docs.title: Malware
docs.text: A built-in panel dashboard for antivirus data: hosts with malware, malware not removed, protection turned off, the top threats and hosts, protection rule blocks and antivirus health problems, across Microsoft Defender, ClamAV and antivirus consoles. It opens on the last 7 days. Until antivirus events arrive it shows a Set up antivirus logs button (for admins) that opens Add data. See antivirus.md for each panel.

docs.title: Vulnerabilities
docs.text: A built-in panel dashboard for the scans on the Vulnerabilities page: hosts with known exploited and critical CVEs, the known exploited CVEs to patch first, the top CVEs, the most vulnerable hosts and software, open services, remote access and cleartext services left open, and the hosts found on each network. It opens on the last 7 days. Until a scan has run it shows an Open Vulnerabilities button.

docs.title: Built-in dashboards are read-only
docs.text:
Built-in dashboards are part of Signalith and change only with it, so they have no Settings, Add panel or panel editing, and the panel menu has only Open in Search. Download YAML saves a built-in dashboard's definition, and works without dashboards.dir.

To change one, choose Make a copy (analysts and admins, when custom dashboards are on). It saves Malware (copy) as a custom dashboard with the same panels and opens it, ready to edit. Add to dashboard on the Search page lists custom dashboards only.

The ids posture, malware and vulnerabilities belong to the built-in dashboards. A file malware.yaml in dashboards.dir is ignored and listed as a problem: rename the file and change its id to keep it.

docs.title: Custom dashboards
docs.text:
A custom dashboard is a list of panels. Each panel is a Signalith query and a way to show its result.

Visualization viz Best for Single value single | stats count or any query whose first row has a number; can show the change from the previous period Table table Any result Bar chart bar | stats count by field, | top field; one bar per row Line chart line | timechart ... Stacked columns area | timechart ...; one column per time bucket, series stacked

Ways to add a panel:

  • From Search. Run a search, then click Add to dashboard. Pick a dashboard (or create one), check the preview and save. If the query came from the plain-English Ask box, the question becomes the panel title.
  • Ask in plain English. In Add panel, type a question such as failed logins by source ip and click Write query. The query is written for you (and by the AI model if one is configured and the question needs it), and a preview runs.
  • Write the query yourself; the visualization is picked from its shape (timechart is a line, stats with no by a single value, other stats and top bars, anything else a table). You can change it.

Click Edit dashboard to rename it, set its default time range and auto-refresh, move panels up and down, remove panels, or delete the dashboard. Edit on a panel changes its query, title, visualization or width. Search on a panel opens its query on the Search page.

Panels run in parallel, four at a time, through the same engine as the Search page. A panel whose query fails shows the error in its own card; the others are not affected. A panel returns at most 500 rows.

docs.title: Where dashboards live
docs.text:
Each custom dashboard is one YAML file, <id>.yaml, in dashboards.dir (default: a dashboards folder next to the config file; /var/lib/signalith/dashboards for the systemd unit and Docker image; SIGNALITH_DASHBOARDS_DIR overrides it). Saving in the UI writes the file. Files are read every time the list or a dashboard is opened, so dashboards you copy in or git pull show up without a restart. A file with mistakes is listed at the top of the Dashboards page with every problem, and signalith validate checks every file.

On the servers of a cluster, custom dashboards are shared: a dashboard saved on any server is the same everywhere, and every server's dashboards folder holds a copy. A file added or changed in a server's folder is shared; removing one changes nothing unless detections.sync is mirror. A save made from a page that read an older version is refused with 412, and the page offers to reload or overwrite. See Shared detections, dashboards and asset lists.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
id: auth-watch              # 3-64 lowercase letters, digits, - or _; must match the file name
title: Authentication watch
description: Failed logons and where they come from    # optional
time_range: 24h             # default range: m, h, d or w; the page's picker overrides it
refresh: 5m                 # optional auto-refresh, at least 30s; empty is off
panels:
  - title: Failed logons
    query: datamodel=Authentication action=failure | stats count
    viz: single
    compare: true           # show the change from the previous period
    width: third            # third, half or full
  - title: Distinct users targeted
    query: datamodel=Authentication action=failure | stats count, dc(user) as users
    viz: single
    field: users            # which column a single value shows (default: the first number)
  - title: Logons over time
    query: |
      datamodel=Authentication
      | timechart count by action
    viz: area
    width: full
  - title: Failures by source
    query: |
      datamodel=Authentication action=failure
      | stats count by src
      | sort -count
      | head 10
    viz: bar
  - title: Accounts created this week
    query: datamodel=Change action=created earliest=-7d | table _time, host, user, object
    viz: table
Key Default Meaning id from the title File name without .yaml. posture, malware and vulnerabilities are reserved for the built-in dashboards title required Shown in the dashboard list description none Shown under the title time_range 24h Default time range for panels refresh off Auto-refresh interval panels[].title required Panel heading panels[].query required Any Signalith query; see query-language.md panels[].viz from the query single, table, bar, line or area panels[].width third for single values, full for line and area, else half Panel width on wide screens; every panel is full width on a phone panels[].field first number Column a single value shows panels[].compare false Single values only: also run the query over the previous period and show the change

A query that sets its own earliest= keeps it whatever the time picker says. compare needs a relative range such as 24h or earliest=-7d; a query with latest= is not compared. Unknown keys are rejected so typos are caught.

docs.title: API
docs.text:
Every endpoint needs the admin sign-in, like the rest of the API.

Endpoint Purpose GET /api/posture?range=24h The security posture report (range 1m to 90d) GET /api/dashboards List: the built-in dashboards (posture, then malware and vulnerabilities, each with "builtin": true, even when custom dashboards are off), every custom one, and files with problems POST /api/dashboards Create; without id, one is made from the title. 409 if the id exists or belongs to a built-in dashboard GET /api/dashboards/{id} One dashboard as JSON GET /api/dashboards/{id}/yaml Download its YAML file PUT /api/dashboards/{id} Replace a dashboard (save edits, reorder panels) DELETE /api/dashboards/{id} Delete its file POST /api/dashboards/{id}/panels Append one panel ({"title", "query", "viz", ...}) POST /api/dashboards/{id}/run Run every panel; body {"range": "7d"} is optional. Returns one result per panel, each with result, value and previous for single values, or error POST /api/panels/run Run an unsaved panel: {"range": "24h", "panel": {...}}

Validation errors return 400 with a problems list naming each field to fix.

GET, /yaml and /run also work for the built-in malware and vulnerabilities dashboards, without dashboards.dir. PUT, DELETE and adding a panel to it return 400: The Malware dashboard is built in and can’t be changed. Make a copy to change it.

docs.title: Detections
docs.text: A detection is a Signalith query that runs on a schedule. Every row the query returns becomes a finding, unless the throttle says the same thing was already raised recently.

docs.title: Where detections live
docs.text:
• Built-in detections ship inside the binary (internal/detect/builtin).
  • Content pack detections ship inside the binary too, off until you turn them on (see Content packs).
  • Custom and edited detections are YAML files in detections.dir (default: a detections folder next to the config file; /var/lib/signalith/detections for the systemd unit and Docker image). One file per detection, named <id>.yaml.
  • A file whose id matches a built-in or pack detection overrides it. Delete the file, or click Revert to built-in, to go back.
  • Turning a built-in or pack detection on or off, or giving it exceptions, without other changes only writes a small file to detections/state/<id>.yaml, so the rule itself keeps coming from the binary and gets fixes on upgrade.

You can edit detections in the UI or drop YAML files into the folder and restart. signalith validate checks every file and reports problems with the field to fix; a broken file is skipped at startup and logged, so it never stops the server.

docs.title: On several servers
docs.text:
The servers of a cluster share their detections: custom ones, overrides, and the choices made for built-in and pack ones. Each server's detections folder is then an inbox: a file added or changed there is shared, and a change made on any server is written back into every server's folder. Removing a file changes nothing unless detections.sync is mirror. See Shared detections, dashboards and asset lists.

Saving a detection sends the version the page read (If-Match with the etag from GET /api/detections/{id}); if someone else saved it meanwhile, the save is refused with 412, naming who changed it, on which server and when.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
id: auth-brute-force                    # 3-64 lowercase letters, digits, - or _
title: Brute force against $dest$ from $src$   # $field$ is filled from the result row
name: Brute force     # optional: the name without $field$ tokens, for counts across hosts
description: One source failed to log on to a system many times.
query: |
  datamodel=Authentication action=failure
  | stats count, dc(user) as users by src, dest
  | where count >= 10
schedule: 5m          # how often it runs: s, m, h, d or w
lookback: 15m         # how far back each run searches
severity: medium      # informational, low, medium, high, critical
mitre: [T1110]        # ATT&CK technique or sub-technique IDs
throttle:
  fields: [src, dest] # one finding per distinct src and dest...
  window: 1h          # ...per hour
risk:                 # optional; see "Risk" below
  score: 30
  objects:
    - {field: src, type: system}
enabled: true
tags: [authentication]
guidance: Check whether the source is internal and whether any attempt succeeded.

Rules of thumb:

  • Do not put earliest= or latest= in the query; lookback sets the window.
  • Make lookback at least as long as schedule, or events between runs are missed. A little overlap is fine; throttling keeps overlapping runs from raising duplicates.
  • Without throttle.fields, the whole result row is the throttle key.
  • Views that count a detection across many findings, such as Top detections firing on the posture dashboard, show name. Without one, they show title with each $field$ and the word that leads to it left out ("Brute force against $dest$ from $src$" reads "Brute force"). Set name when that reads badly, as for a title that starts with a $field$.
  • Use stats ... by to raise one finding per entity instead of one per event.
  • Up to four detections run at once. A run is stopped when it takes longer than its schedule (at least 1 minute, at most 5); the Detections page then shows Timed out. Narrow the query or shorten lookback so it finishes in time.

docs.title: Schedules and missed runs
docs.text:
• Fixed times. Each detection runs at fixed times: every schedule, at a moment Signalith picks for that rule, so that rules with the same schedule do not all start together. Every server works these times out the same way, from OpenSearch's clock.
  • What a run searches. Each run searches the lookback that ends at its scheduled time, even when it starts a little late.
  • Missed runs are made up. When runs are missed, because every worker was busy or no server was running detections, they are run later, oldest first, so nothing in between goes unsearched. They are made up as far back as detections.catch_up (default 6h, at most 7d; 0 turns this off and runs only the latest time). Older missed runs are skipped: the Detections page marks the detection Skipped, and its details and the posture dashboard say for which times, for example "Signalith was not running detections from 02:10 to 09:40; 90 runs of this detection were skipped." Search that time by hand if it matters. Set detections.catch_up on the Settings page, or see the configuration table.
  • Failed runs. A run that failed because OpenSearch did not answer, or was too busy, is tried again: the detection waits until it works. A run whose query has an error is not tried again; fix the query and the next run uses it. A run that times out is tried up to three times, then the next one goes on.
  • New, turned on again, or rescheduled. A new detection, one turned back on, and one whose schedule changed start at their next scheduled time; they do not make up the time before it. Changing only the query or lookback keeps the place in the schedule.
  • After upgrading. The first time this version starts, each detection that is on runs once straight away, over the lookback up to its latest scheduled time, as every start did before. From then on it keeps to its schedule.
  • Times on findings. A finding's Detected time is the scheduled time of the run that raised it, so a run made up later still sorts where it belongs. A finding raised more than a few minutes after that time also says how much later it was raised (hold the pointer over it for the exact time).
  • No duplicates. A run that is repeated, for example after a restart or when another server takes the detections over, finds what it raised before and does not raise it again. Throttling also holds across servers and restarts.
  • Run now searches the lookback up to this moment, on the server you are using, whichever server runs the schedule. It respects throttling and its findings throttle the scheduled runs in turn, but it does not change the schedule. The detection's details show it as Last run now, with who ran it and where.
  • The Detections page shows late runs and skipped runs under Behind schedule, and the Health page warns while a detection waits longer than its schedule, and for a day after runs were skipped.

docs.title: Risk
docs.text:
A risk section makes the detection add risk to the users and systems in each result row:

Key Meaning score Base risk, 1 to 1000. Multiplied by the object's priority from the asset and identity lists (critical ×2, high ×1.5, medium ×1, low ×0.5; a watchlisted user at least ×1.5) objects Result fields that hold a risk object, each with type user, system or other. Empty or missing values are skipped only true records risk without raising a finding. Throttling still applies, per risk object row weight_field A result column with a number from 0 to 10 that multiplies score, such as threat_weight from threatmatch

Each object gets one risk event in the Risk data model with risk_object, risk_object_type, risk_score, risk_base_score, risk_priority, risk_message (the rendered title), detection_id, mitre and mitre_tactic, plus the row's entity fields. Search them with datamodel=Risk.

Ten built-in detections are risk-only. Two risk incident detections (tagged risk-incident) read the Risk data model and raise findings:

  • risk-threshold-exceeded: total risk of 100 or more for one object in 24 hours.
  • risk-multiple-tactics: three or more ATT&CK tactics from three or more detections on one object in 7 days.

The threat intel match detection (threat-activity, tagged threat-intel) runs * | threatmatch every 5 minutes over the last 10, raises one finding per indicator and target system per day, and adds 60 risk times the indicator's weight to threat_target and user. See threat-intel.md.

Write your own the same way, for example datamodel=Risk risk_object_type=user | stats sum(risk_score) as risk_score by risk_object | where risk_score >= 200.

docs.title: Exceptions
docs.text:
An exception tunes a detection without editing its query, like a suppression in Splunk Enterprise Security: results that match it raise no finding and add no risk, and every other result still alerts. Use one for a vulnerability scanner that trips a brute force rule, an admin script that looks like an attack, or a maintenance window.

  • From a finding: admins open the finding, choose More actions (⋯) > Don't alert on this again, tick the values to match (the finding's host, user and so on), pick how long (24 hours, 7 days, 30 days or until removed), and add a comment. The finding can be closed in the same step, as a false positive by default, and its activity records what was suppressed.
  • On the detection: the Exceptions section of a detection lists each exception with who added it, when and why, and how long it lasts. Admins remove one with its bin icon, or add one by hand with Add: one field=value per line, where * and ? are wildcards and case is ignored. Leave the values empty, with a start time and how long, to silence every result for a maintenance window.

Each run counts the results exceptions matched; Last run on the Detections page shows them. An exception that has ended stays listed, greyed out, until it is removed. A detection can have up to 500 exceptions, each matching up to 8 fields.

In YAML (a custom detection keeps them in its own file; a built-in or pack detection in detections/state/<id>.yaml):

exceptions:
  - id: ex-3f9a1c2b7d10
    match: {src: 203.0.113.9}           # every field must match; * and ? are wildcards
    until: 2026-11-01T00:00:00Z          # optional: without it, until removed
    comment: Quarterly vulnerability scan
    by: admin
    added: 2026-10-13T21:00:00Z
  - id: ex-maintenance
    from: 2026-10-18T02:00:00Z           # no match: every result, so until is required
    until: 2026-10-18T06:00:00Z
    comment: Patch window
