Fluent Bit on the manager The manager's syslog output Install Fluent Bit on the manager nothing Transport HTTPS to /api/ingest, checking Signalith's certificate syslog over UDP, unencrypted Buffering kept on disk and sent again if Signalith is down none: alerts sent while Signalith is unreachable are lost Long alerts up to 1 MB each very long alerts can be cut short (see below)

docs.title: Fluent Bit on the Wazuh manager
docs.text:
Open Add data, pick Wazuh and follow the steps. In short, on the machine that runs the Wazuh manager:

  1. Install Fluent Bit 3.1 or later from its signed package repository, following the steps for your distribution at https://docs.fluentbit.io/manual/installation/linux.
  2. Save Signalith's CA certificate as signalith-ca.pem (when Signalith uses HTTPS).
  3. Save the generated configuration as fluent-bit.conf.
  4. Put both in place: sudo install -m 644 -o root -g root signalith-ca.pem /etc/fluent-bit/signalith-ca.pem && sudo install -m 600 -o root -g root fluent-bit.conf /etc/fluent-bit/fluent-bit.conf
  5. Restart Fluent Bit: sudo systemctl enable --now fluent-bit && sudo systemctl restart fluent-bit

The configuration tails the file the manager writes its alerts to, one JSON alert per line, and sends each line with the tag wazuh. The page fills in the address, ingest token and certificate checks; the input part looks like this:

[INPUT]
    Name                 tail
    Tag                  wazuh
    Path                 /var/ossec/logs/alerts/alerts.json
    DB                   /var/lib/fluent-bit/signalith-wazuh.db
    Buffer_Chunk_Size    64k
    Buffer_Max_Size      1M
    Skip_Long_Lines      On
    storage.type         filesystem

alerts.json is written when <jsonout_output>yes</jsonout_output> is set under <global> in the manager's /var/ossec/etc/ossec.conf, which is the default. Fluent Bit runs as root, so it can read the file; it follows the file when the manager rotates it each day.

If Fluent Bit already runs on the manager for something else, add the [INPUT] above and the [OUTPUT] from the generated file to your own configuration instead. Keep the tag wazuh: it is how Signalith knows the lines are Wazuh alerts.

docs.title: The manager's syslog output (no agent)
docs.text:
The Wazuh manager can send each alert as JSON over syslog to Signalith's syslog receiver. In /var/ossec/etc/ossec.conf on the manager, add:

<ossec_config>
  <syslog_output>
    <server>192.168.1.20</server>
    <port>514</port>
    <format>json</format>
  </syslog_output>
</ossec_config>

with Signalith's address as server (the Syslog option on Add data shows it), then turn on the manager's syslog client and restart it:

sudo /var/ossec/bin/wazuh-control enable client-syslog
sudo systemctl restart wazuh-manager

Add <level>7</level> inside <syslog_output> to send only alerts of that rule level and above.

Signalith recognizes a syslog message whose text is a Wazuh JSON alert (an object with rule and agent) and maps it exactly like an alert sent by Fluent Bit. host is the Wazuh agent the alert is about, and dvc is the manager that sent it.

The manager sends syslog over UDP, unencrypted and without retries, so use this route on a network you trust. Very long alerts (with a long full_log) can be cut short by the manager's syslog output; a cut alert is not valid JSON, so it is stored as a plain syslog event (searchable by its text, but not mapped). The Fluent Bit route does not have this limit.

docs.title: How alerts are mapped
docs.text:
Every Wazuh alert gets these fields, whatever model it lands in:

Field From the alert _time timestamp host, dest agent.name signature_id rule.id signature rule.description vendor_product Wazuh sourcetype wazuh:alerts _raw the whole alert, as JSON mitre, mitre_tactic rule.mitre.id, rule.mitre.tactic (lists) wazuh_rule_level rule.level (0 to 15) wazuh_rule_groups rule.groups (a list) wazuh_agent_id, wazuh_agent_name, wazuh_agent_ip agent.id, agent.name, agent.ip wazuh_manager manager.name wazuh_decoder decoder.name wazuh_location location, such as /var/log/auth.log or EventChannel

Then the alert goes to the first model that fits:

Filesystem: file integrity monitoring (syscheck) alerts.

Field From the alert action syscheck.event: added becomes created; modified, deleted file_path, file_name syscheck.path, and its last part file_hash syscheck.sha256_after, lower case file_size syscheck.size_after user syscheck.audit.user.name (who-data), else syscheck.uname_after (the file's owner) process_path, process_name, process_id syscheck.audit.process.name, its file name, syscheck.audit.process.id

Registry: syscheck alerts about Windows registry keys and values (rule group syscheck_registry, or a path starting with HKEY_): action, registry_path, registry_key_name, registry_value_name (syscheck.value_name), user and process as above.

Configuration_Check: Security Configuration Assessment results (data.sca.type is check).

Field From the alert check_id data.sca.check.id check data.sca.check.title result data.sca.check.result (or status on older managers): passed is pass, failed is fail, not applicable is n/a reference data.sca.check.compliance, such as cis: 5.2.8; pci_dss_v4.0: 7.2.1 detail data.sca.check.reason benchmark data.sca.policy, the policy name

rule_id is left empty: it is for SCAP Security Guide rules. SCA scan summaries go to Alerts.

Windows events (data.win.system): Signalith's own Windows parser reads them, from the event data Wazuh sends by name, so they get the same fields as events from Fluent Bit on Windows: 4624 and 4625 logons go to Authentication, 4688 process creation to Endpoint, account and group changes (4720, 4726, 4728, 4732, 4756) to Change, and Sysmon 1 and 3 to Endpoint and Network_Traffic. The Windows event ID is kept in wazuh_win_event_id. Other Windows events continue below.

Authentication: alerts whose rule groups include authentication_success, authentication_failed, authentication_failures or invalid_login (sshd, PAM, sudo, su, Windows and others).

Field From the alert action success or failure, from the rule group app decoder.parent, else decoder.name, such as sshd or pam user data.dstuser, else data.srcuser, else data.win.eventdata.targetUserName src_user data.srcuser, when it differs from data.dstuser (sudo, su) src, src_port data.srcip, data.srcport (Windows: ipAddress, ipPort)

Malware: antivirus alerts, so they are found with every other antivirus's (see the Malware dashboard):

  • Wazuh's ClamAV integration (rule groups clamd or freshclam): the ClamAV message in full_log is read like a ClamAV log, giving signature, file_path, action and, for definition updates, type=health. vendor_product is ClamAV.
  • VirusTotal matches (data.virustotal.malicious is 1): signature says how many engines flagged the file, with file_path, file_md5, file_sha1 and the report in url.
  • Rootcheck's trojaned files: category=trojan, with the file from data.file or full_log. Other rootcheck findings go to Alerts.

The rule's description is kept in description, and severity comes from rule.level as for Alerts (0 to 3 counts as low).

Alerts: everything else.

Field From the alert app wazuh id id, the alert's own ID description rule.description severity from rule.level: 0 to 3 informational, 4 to 6 low, 7 to 9 medium, 10 to 12 high, 13 to 15 critical severity_id rule.level type rule.groups, joined with commas src data.srcip user data.dstuser, else data.srcuser, else the Windows target or subject user

Anything not mapped stays in _raw, so you can still find it by text, for example sourcetype=wazuh:alerts "Trojaned version".

docs.title: Checking it works
docs.text:
Search sourcetype=wazuh:alerts over the last hour. To see what kinds of alerts arrive:

sourcetype=wazuh:alerts | stats count by datamodel, signature

A line under the wazuh tag that is not a Wazuh alert is kept in Other with sourcetype wazuh:alerts. If nothing arrives, check the Health page and Fluent Bit's log (journalctl -u fluent-bit) on the manager; for the syslog route, the Syslog option on Add data shows the messages arriving from the manager.
